evidences.title: Amir Khan fights back after 'overrated' jibe from Danny Garca's father | Amir Khan | The Guardian
evidences.content:
Amir Khan has promised to beat Danny Garca after his next opponent's father claimed the former world champion was overrated ahead of their 14 July meeting.

Garca will face Khan at the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas after the latter's rematch with Lamont Peterson fell through when the American tested positive for testosterone. Peterson had become the WBA and IBF light welterweight champion when he beat Khan by a controversial split decision in his native Washington in December.

Garca's father Angel told a press conference in Los Angeles: "Khan is an overrated fighter. Peterson whupped him like an octopus and then he blamed it on the judges."

Garca took the WBC light welterweight title off Erik Morales and will now put the belt on the line against Khan, with both fighters managed by Golden Boy Promotions.

Following the taunts by Garca's father, Khan said: "Danny's father does a lot of talking, but at the end of the day he's not the one who's going to be in the ring. When I beat your son am I still going to be overrated? We will see what happens."

Khan has something to prove following the defeat to Peterson but does not underestimate the challenge he faces against Garca.

"After the Peterson fight fell through we were quite desperate to get a fight because I was at my peak. Danny accepted the challenge. I know how good he is. He's had a good win against Erik Morales. This is going to be a big test for me."

Garca said: "Khan's a great fighter, I'm a great fighter. When you put two great fighters together you get an awesome show. I'm ready to defend my title."
